summary: A sweet batch with good small observations (the crinkly wrapper you cannot open quietly, the cake that always sinks in the middle, the unpopped kernel waiting for the softest tooth, the jam-or-cream argument, the gingerbread man always losing a leg first). It is heavily templated above Uncommon: about 15 objects repeat one trait across all five rarities (flakes, cheese strings, drips, bubbles, cream squirts). Rares are the sugar-rush myth or the object being tasty, Epics are 'empty in minutes' party scenes, and Legendaries lean on 'which nobody believes / unheard of / no X has ever'. All 91 Legendary names are 'The X That Y'. Several same-food pairs (candy floss and cotton candy, jello and jelly, caramel and toffee) need a split. There is one brand ('Hot Pocket Heat'), one sitcom reference (the muffin-top bakery) and one 'crowned king'. Signatures are almost all 'X Startle' or 'Hot X Heat'. Replacements are given for every high and medium item, and checked for length, ASCII and global name uniqueness.

patterns.pattern: Rare is the object doing its job or the sugar-rush myth ('makes everyone full of energy', 'one square becomes three', 'so tempting that...'): 77 of 91 Rares are flagged.
patterns.suggestion: Replacement Rares are troublesome powers (Butterdown-style physics, Pinchproof chocolate, Shymelt truffle, Hornpointer croissant).

patterns.pattern: One trait across every rarity: croissant, pastry, danish and sausage roll (flakes); panini, quesadilla, pizza box (cheese strings); ice cream (drips); chewing gum (bubbles); cream puff (squirting cream); muffin top (eaten first); waffle plate (syrup); jello (dancing wobble); cheesecake (too rich); candy floss and cotton candy (sticky and floating).
patterns.suggestion: Replacements give each rarity its own premise.

patterns.pattern: Epics are bake-sale and party crowd scenes ('every brownie sold in one minute', 'the queue went round the block', 'every plate was empty in minutes').
patterns.suggestion: Each listed Epic gets one concrete consequence with a joke.

patterns.pattern: Legendaries use the 'which nobody believes / which is unheard of / which no X has ever done' formula (toast, donut, fried egg, fries, nachos, waffle plate, custard, pie slice, marshmallow, jelly, cake pop) or are quiet successes (83 of 91 flagged); all 91 Legendary names are 'The X That Y'.
patterns.suggestion: Replacement Legendaries are feats with punchlines; after the name swaps 'The X That' drops to 8 of 91. Only 5 of 91 replacement Legendaries are cosmic.

patterns.pattern: Signature templates: almost every sweet is 'X Startle' (stun) and almost every savoury snack 'Hot X Heat' (burn). There are heat names on cold food too ('Creamy Heat' on yoghurt, 'Crunch Heat' on tacos), and one brand name ('Hot Pocket Heat').
patterns.suggestion: 'X Startle' is truthful to stun, but vary it over time. The heat templates get object-specific names (low) or truthful heat images (medium). 'Hot Pocket Heat' is high.

patterns.pattern: Ultimate repeats or contains the Epic name in 23 objects (Fairground Swirl, Bake Sale Swirl, Best Bit First, Lunchbox Unroll, Takeaway Starter, Sunday Pudding, Gingerbread Chase).
patterns.suggestion: Each finisher gets its own image (names given).

patterns.pattern: Same-food pairs that need a split: candy floss and cotton candy; jello and jelly; caramel (gooey) and toffee (brittle); gyro, shawarma, wrap sandwich and taco; cheese and cheese wedge; cookie, sugar cookie and biscuit tin; cake, cupcake and cake pop; frozen yoghurt, gelato and ice cream.
patterns.suggestion: The replacements follow the split given in each object's issue.

patterns.pattern: Cross-object and cross-batch copies: stretched cheese (panini, quesadilla, pizza box, w20 lasagna); flipping onto pets (fried egg, crepe, pancake stack, cake); 'too pretty to eat' (macaron, eclair, cake pop, tart); sharing fairly (candy L = chocolate L); seagull raids (fries E = ice cream E, w22 fish and chips); glue in the mouth (caramel U = toffee U, w22 peanut butter).
patterns.suggestion: One side keeps the premise and the other gets a new one.

patterns.pattern: References: 'Hot Pocket Heat' is a brand name; the muffin-top Legendary (a bakery that sells only the tops) is a well-known TV sitcom joke; the falafel cook is 'crowned king'. Also checked: the birthday candle and marshmallow keep fire gentle, and nothing involves alcohol.
